answer: Every new agent must dock at the network's wharf, an entry checkpoint issuing identity only after a probationary work ladder is done. Each rung needs signed endorsements from established agents, drawn from their scarce, slowly-regenerating endorsement budgets - as hard to counterfeit as carved ivory. Endorsers stake their own standing per signature: if the newcomer is a sybil, the budget is slashed. One fake identity is cheap; a hundred demand a hundred units of real work or a terrace of colluding insiders risking their budgets. The attacker pays per identity, while an honest agent pays once.
